entries.rationale: Directly writing to a production file risks corruption if the process crashes. Using mktemp + mv ensures atomic consistency.

entries.good_example:
patch_file() {
    local target="$1" start="$2" end="$3" temp=$(mktemp)
    sed -n "1,/$start/p" "$target" > "$temp"
    cat >> "$temp" # Injects from stdin
    sed -n "/$end/,$ p" "$target" >> "$temp"
    mv "$temp" "$target"
}
entries.rationale: Regex substitution (sed -i) is brittle and hard to read for multi-line blocks. The SS QLM pattern uses markers and Heredocs for clear, block-based modifications.
Scripts relying on relative paths fail when called from different directories. Resolving the absolute script origin is mandatory for stability.
